title: Multiplication by $d$ prime to the characteristic is etale
statement:
Let $A$ be an abelian variety of dimension $g$ over a field $k$
and let $d\geq1$. If $\operatorname{char}k\nmid d$, then the
multiplication morphism $[d]:A\to A$ of [def-sc-mult-n] is etale,
and its kernel $A[d]$ is a finite etale group scheme of rank
$d^{2g}$ (equivalently, it has order $d^{2g}$).
(*Stacks Project, Groupoid Schemes, [Tag 0BFH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BFH)*.)

proof.text: The morphism [d] is a homomorphism of group schemes. By translation invariance of the etale locus for a homomorphism [lem-sc-hom-etale-locus-translation], it is enough to check etaleness at the identity e.

The finite-flat input [lem-sc-mult-n-finite-flat] makes [d] finite locally free. The finite-flat tangent criterion [lem-sc-finite-flat-unramified-tangent-criterion] identifies etaleness at e with injectivity of the tangent map d[d] on T_{A/k,e}.

The differential of the group addition is additive on tangent vectors [lem-sc-group-addition-tangent-differential], and hence the differential of [d] is scalar multiplication v↦d·v [lem-sc-mult-n-tangent-differential]. Since char(k) does not divide d, this scalar map is injective. Thus [d] is etale.

The kernel A[d] is the base change of [d] along the identity section e:Spec(k)→A. The one-member family ([d]) is etale and surjective (a finite locally free morphism of rank d^{2g}≥1 is surjective), so by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] applied with g=e its base change A[d]→Spec(k) is etale; thus A[d] is etale; [lem-sc-mult-n-finite-flat] gives that it is finite and has rank d^{2g}.
